subject: AuroraPay: IR artifacts request and L3 review coordination
messages:
From: Lina Park <lina.park@aurorapay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@aurorapay.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Suspicious auth behavior / artifacts request

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the quick call earlier. Per our security team, we need the following from Redwood to complete our SIG/SOC2 evidence review for the integration:

- Incident response timeline for the suspected session anomalies (UTC timestamps)
- Sample auth logs and SSO assertion payloads (redact PII)
- Copy of the IR runbook or playbook steps you followed during the investigation
- Confirmation of data retention policy for auth logs and KV cache (retention period + storage location)

Can you provide a consolidated bundle by EOD Monday 11/8? Our compliance deadline is tight; if you need an NDA or limited sharing channel let us know.

Lina Park
Sr. Security Operations Manager
AuroraPay

Team — forwarding AuroraPay's ask. They want a consolidated evidence bundle for SIG/SOC2 review by EOD 11/08. Quick notes:

- This is high priority (legal + procurement on the thread).
- We need L3 to validate logs we plan to share and confirm redaction approach.
- Marissa, can you own assembling the bundle and verify which artifacts are safe to share under the standard customer disclosure?
- Karthik, please generate an IR timeline (UTC) and a short summary of mitigation steps taken. Include references to runbook sections that triggered.
- Neha, confirm retention policy wording and whether any keys/metrics are excluded from exports.

I'll coordinate export access and a secure Drive share; don't upload raw auth archives to public folders.

Thanks — Jordan
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Jordan / team — quick checklist and plan:

1) Evidence bundle (I will assemble):
   - ir_timeline.csv (UTC, event_id, actor, action, sample_token_id)
   - auth-logs-20261105.tar.gz (sample subset; PII redacted)
   - runbook-snippets.pdf (exported sections 3.1–3.5 detailing escalation + mitigation)
   - sig-mapping.xlsx (mapping of requested SIG items to our controls/evidence)

2) Sanitation & scope:
   - We will remove IPs where customer explicitly requested masking and replace with x.x.x.x placeholders.
   - No full keys or secrets will be included; any KMS references will be descriptive only.

3) L3 review: Karthik, can you validate the auth log sample and sign off on redaction by 11/07 11:00 PST? We need the sign-off before I package.

4) Delivery: Jordan — please set up a secure Drive folder with restricted access and an expiring link (7 days). I will upload final ZIP and attach a manifest.

I'll start drafting the manifest and include a short cover note for AuroraPay's compliance team.

Marissa
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Suspicious auth behavior / artifacts request

Marissa / Jordan / Neha — signing off on the artifacts. Summary of what I reviewed:

- ir_timeline.csv: produced (UTC) with event_ids, correlating request_ids; I removed three rows containing customer email addresses and replaced them with redaction tokens (REDACTED_EMAIL_x).
- auth-logs-20261105.tar.gz: sample subset includes 24 hours of auth events for the affected tenant. I verified assertions for SAML flows; replaced raw assertion.saml with a summarized XML extract (assertion-excerpt.txt) that preserves timestamps and subject IDs only.
- runbook-snippets.pdf: highlighted the exact subsection we executed (Runbook §3.4 — Session Anomaly Handling).
- sig-mapping.xlsx: mapped SIG questions to our control artifacts and included page/slide refs.

Risks / notes:
- There is a transient telemetry spike correlated with a third-party identity provider failure; we included that context in the timeline.
- Retention policy: auth logs are retained 90 days in encrypted S3; we included a short policy extract and the storage bucket name in the manifest.

I've uploaded the validated artifacts to the secure Drive folder Jordan created (link below). Please review the manifest and cover note; once OK I'll share with Lina and CC procurement as requested.

Karthik
L3 Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
